ProgramName: Master of Science in Athletic Training

Description:
Kent State University’s Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) program provides a comprehensive professional education in athletic training. Our program is designed to develop athletic trainers that are reflective, skilled, and professional practitioners. The program features a rigorous curriculum, hands-on immersive clinical experiences, and an applied research project, providing you with the skills and knowledge to excel in diverse healthcare settings. This program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE) and prepares graduates to be eligible for the Board of Certification (BOC) exam.

The Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) program at Kent State University provides students with a dynamic, immersive learning environment. Here’s what sets our program apart:
*   Comprehensive Curriculum: Our curriculum integrates foundational sciences, clinical skills, and evidence-based practices to ensure you gain a holistic understanding of athletic training.
*   Immersive Clinical Experiences: Gain hands-on experience in diverse clinical settings, including intercollegiate athletics, high schools, outpatient clinics, and physician offices. You’ll work alongside experienced clinicians and apply classroom knowledge to real-world scenarios.
*   Expert Faculty: Learn from dedicated faculty members who are experts in their fields, committed to your academic and professional growth.
*   Research Opportunities: Engage in applied research projects, contributing to the advancement of athletic training knowledge and developing critical inquiry skills.
*   Professional Development: Our program emphasizes professional ethics, interprofessional collaboration, and leadership development, preparing you for a successful career in healthcare.

Upon completion of the Master of Science in Athletic Training program, graduates will be able to:
*   Demonstrate competence in foundational and advanced athletic training knowledge and skills.
*   Apply evidence-based practice principles to clinical decision-making.
*   Exhibit professional behaviors and ethical conduct in all aspects of practice.
*   Collaborate effectively with healthcare professionals and patients.
*   Critically evaluate research and integrate findings into clinical practice.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE)

Description: The three-year Master of Fine Arts in Acting program at Kent State University is a rigorous, demanding program designed to prepare talented and dedicated individuals for professional careers in theatre, film, and television. A small cohort of highly selective graduate students work with our internationally recognized faculty in a vibrant and supportive atmosphere that fosters both artistic and personal growth. Our approach to training is rooted in Stanislavski-based techniques, but also includes a diverse palette of contemporary and classical acting methods and pedagogies. We are proud to be members of the University/Resident Theatre Association (U/RTA) and The National Alliance of Acting Teachers. Through an intensive array of classes, productions, and workshops, students will hone their skills in voice, speech, movement, stage combat, acting for the camera, Shakespeare, and other relevant areas. The program culminates in a New York City showcase, providing students with direct exposure to industry professionals. Our alumni have gone on to perform on Broadway, off-Broadway, in regional theatres, and in film and television roles. Many have also become successful educators and theatre practitioners.

Description:
The Post-Master’s Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner is designed for nurses who have already completed a master’s degree in nursing and who desire to become certified as an adult-gerontology primary care nurse practitioner. The program will provide the knowledge and skills necessary for the advanced practice role of the adult-gerontology primary care nurse practitioner and will prepare students to sit for the national certification examination for this role.
The Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner is an advanced practice nurse who provides primary care to adolescents (13 years of age and older) through the entire adult life span, including the elderly. They promote health and provide care for common acute and chronic illnesses within a primary care setting. The curriculum provides a strong theoretical and clinical base in advanced health assessment, pathophysiology, pharmacology, differential diagnosis and disease management.
Upon completion of the Post-Master’s Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, graduates are eligible to take the national certification examination provided by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) or the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners (AANP).

Description: The Graduate Certificate in Adult/Adolescent Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) program is a post-master's certificate for master's prepared registered nurses or those enrolled in a master's program. The program is offered in a hybrid format, including didactic coursework, hands-on clinical simulation experiences, and clinical practicum hours. SANE nurses provide compassionate, expert care to patients who have experienced sexual assault. With the number of sexual assault victims on the rise, the need for qualified SANE nurses has never been greater. Kent State University is the only program in Northeast Ohio that offers graduate-level SANE education. The SANE program combines didactic coursework, clinical simulation experiences, and clinical practicum hours in a hybrid format. Students will learn the critical skills needed to provide trauma-informed care for patients who have experienced sexual assault and other forms of interpersonal violence. Students will also learn how to conduct forensic evidence collection, participate in legal proceedings, and provide crisis intervention and support to victims.

Statement of purpose addressing interest in the program and intended research area. Curriculum vitae or resume. Three letters of recommendation. Writing sample (typically a research paper or term paper from an undergraduate course). English language proficiency — international applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency (unless waived). GRE scores are not required.

Graduates of the program are well prepared for doctoral programs in anthropology or for careers in cultural resource management, museums, forensic anthropology, public health or international development.

Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, government agencies, environmental consulting firms, and private industry.

Graduates of this program will be able to: Apply advanced mathematical concepts and techniques to solve real-world problems. Develop and implement mathematical models to analyze complex systems. ProgramName: Master of Architecture

The program emphasizes artistic inquiry, research, and critical thinking within the context of current issues in art education. Graduates of the program are prepared to assume leadership positions as highly qualified art teachers and advocates for art education. The program offers both on-campus and fully online options.

The program offers both thesis and non-thesis options, allowing students to tailor their academic path to their individual goals. Graduates are prepared for doctoral studies, careers in museums, galleries, academia or other art-related fields.

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program in Biomedical Sciences is based on a holistic review of all application materials. Requirements include: online application, application fee, official transcripts, a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, and official GRE scores (general test) for applicants who do not have a master's degree in a relevant area, or have a master's degree in a relevant area with a GPA below 3.5 on a 4.0 scale. International applicants must submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. The application requires applicants to list their research, publications and other relevant experience; therefore, a CV is highly recommended.
Description: The Human Evolutionary Biology (HEB) concentration focuses on the study of human and primate evolution from a comparative perspective, investigating the biological and behavioral processes that characterize humans and their primate relatives. Faculty research interests include hominin paleontology, evolutionary morphology, primate behavioral ecology, human behavioral ecology, primate conservation and evolutionary medicine. Students are trained to conduct interdisciplinary research within the department and in collaboration with colleagues across campus. Research opportunities include fieldwork at fossil sites in Kenya and Tanzania, analyses of existing fossil and primate skeletal collections and behavioral studies of captive primates. Research in the HEB concentration leverages close ties with the Kent State University Museum and with the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
CostPerCredit: $658.90/credit hour (Ohio Resident), $1241.30/credit hour (Non-Ohio Resident)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences
Requirements: Admission to the M.S. in Biomedical Sciences with a concentration in Neuroscience requires an undergraduate degree in a science-related discipline with a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Arts and Sciences. In addition, applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose, A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV), Official GRE scores
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences is offered to students with diverse backgrounds in biological and physical sciences who are interested in pursuing research careers in biomedical sciences or allied health professions. This program provides students with fundamental knowledge in biomedical sciences while offering advanced courses and research training in specialized areas. Graduates are prepared for doctoral studies in biomedical sciences, medical school or other health professional programs and positions in academic or industrial research.
CostPerCredit: $608.20/credit

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences
Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences program with a concentration in Neurosciences requires the following: A minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale for baccalaureate coursework and a minimum 3.000 GPA for graduate coursework. Official transcripts. Statement of purpose that describes the applicant’s academic and research experience, research interests and reasons for applying to the Neurosciences program. Curriculum vitae (CV). Three letters of recommendation. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency (unless exempt). The GRE general test is not required. Admission decisions are based on a holistic review of all application materials.
Description: The Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences with a concentration in Neurosciences program focuses on fundamental and translational research in brain function and dysfunction, with an emphasis on molecular, cellular, anatomical, physiological and behavioral mechanisms. The program prepares students for careers in academic research, government or industry. Students in this program are trained in multiple areas of neuroscience, including molecular, cellular, systems and behavioral neuroscience, and are expected to develop an individualized research program, write grant proposals, publish scientific articles and present at national meetings.
CostPerCredit: $1,069/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Pharmacology
Requirements: Applicants for admission to the master's program must have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. All applicants are required to take the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Official transcripts. Three letters of recommendation. International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency.
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences focuses on research-intensive training and career preparation in biomedical research. The Biomedical Sciences program offers concentrations in Cell and Molecular Biology, Neuroscience, Pharmacology and Physiology. The Pharmacology concentration prepares students for careers in research or academia at universities, pharmaceutical companies or government agencies. The concentration provides students with foundational training in pharmacology, including pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics and toxicology, as well-as hands-on research experience.
CostPerCredit: $1,288/credit hour (Non-Resident graduate)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Physiology Interdisciplinary
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Graduate Studies, as published in the Graduate Catalog.
A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA.
Minimum 3.000 GPA in biomedical sciences courses.
Official transcripts.
Three letters of recommendation.
A curriculum vitae.
A statement of purpose regarding academic and career goals.
Official GRE general test scores.
Department: College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Biological Sciences
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in biomedical research or further study in doctoral programs in biomedical sciences and health professional schools. The M.S. degree requires students to acquire knowledge in biomedical sciences through graduate-level coursework and develop skills in scientific research through the completion of a thesis. The program offers three interdisciplinary concentrations: Cellular and Molecular Biology, Neuroscience and Physiology. The program is offered on the Kent campus and at the Northeast Ohio Medical University (NEOMED). The Physiology Interdisciplinary concentration focuses on the study of the function of living systems and their components, ranging from the molecular and cellular level to integrated systems physiology, which is applicable to many health-related professions and research areas. The program provides a broad curriculum covering topics such as cardiovascular, renal, neuro- and respiratory physiology, endocrinology, metabolism and immunology. The program includes coursework, seminars and mentored research experiences that provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue doctoral studies, enter health professional schools or work in biomedical research.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $620/Credit Hour, Non-Ohio Resident: $1123/Credit Hour (2023-2024)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Graduate Assistantships, Fellowships, Grants

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: Admission to the M.S. degree in Chemistry requires a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry or an allied field, with an undergraduate minimum 2.750 overall GPA on a 4.000 point scale. Applicants are encouraged to submit three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic and/or research abilities. A statement of purpose is required, briefly outlining the applicant's research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in chemistry. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or resume. All applicants are required to take the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test. While there is no minimum GRE score required for admission, applicants are encouraged to score at or above the 50th percentile in the Quantitative and Verbal sections of the GRE. The Analytical Writing section of the GRE is not required. GRE scores should be sent directly to Kent State University (Code 1367). An interview (in person or via video conference) may be required. For international students, proof of English Language Proficiency (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS) is also required.
Description: The Master of Science in Chemistry degree program prepares students for careers in chemical industries and related fields or for further graduate study toward a Ph.D. in Chemistry. The program emphasizes both advanced coursework and original research. Thesis and non-thesis options are available.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition waiver (valued at approximately $12,685/year for Ohio residents or $22,959/year for non-Ohio residents based on 18 credits) plus a minimum stipend of $16,000 for 9-month assistantships.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science degree in Computer Science is granted to students who hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and satisfy the following requirements:
Undergraduate major in computer science or a related discipline. Applicants with an undergraduate major in an unrelated discipline must complete prerequisite undergraduate coursework.
Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale (for unconditional admission).
Submission of official GRE scores is highly recommended. Students with GRE General Test scores of at least 300 (verbal + quantitative) and a 3.0 analytical writing score are eligible for admission consideration without additional evaluation of academic preparedness.
Three letters of recommendation are required.
A statement of purpose is required.
A resume or curriculum vitae is required.
Concentration: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Bioinformatics, Data Science, Software Engineering
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Computer Science is a research-oriented program offering advanced study in computer science. The program curriculum includes advanced coursework, seminars, comprehensive examinations and original research. Thesis and non-thesis options are available. The thesis option focuses on advanced research and culminates in the preparation and defense of a master's thesis. The non-thesis option focuses on advanced coursework and requires a comprehensive examination. Students completing the M.S. degree are prepared for positions in industry, research and development, or for further graduate study in a doctoral program.
CostPerCredit: $1,380.40/credit hour
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, University Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Computer Science
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts in Computer Science program requires a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the requirements of the Graduate College and submit additional program materials.
*   Official Transcripts: Transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework must be submitted.
*   GPA: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 in computer science courses.
*   GRE: Applicants are not required to submit GRE scores for admission.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities.
*   Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic and career goals and how the M.A. program will help achieve them.
*   Resume/Curriculum Vitae: A current resume or curriculum vitae.
*   International Applicants: Additional requirements for international applicants.
Conditional Admission: Applicants who do not meet all criteria may be considered for conditional admission on a case-by-case basis.
Description: The Master of Arts in Computer Science degree is offered through the Department of Computer Science. The program prepares students to meet the demand for advanced knowledge in computer science. Students develop skills in areas such as algorithms, artificial intelligence, computer architecture, computer graphics, computer networks, database systems, distributed computing, operating systems, programming languages, software engineering and theoretical computer science. Graduate students are trained for positions in business, industry, education and government. The M.A. in Computer Science program is excellent preparation for doctoral study.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice

All applicants must meet the university admission requirements as well as the following program admission requirements:

*   Resume/curriculum vitae (CV)

The program curriculum includes coursework in criminological theory, research methods, advanced statistics, and electives in areas such as policing, corrections, victimization, juvenile delinquency, race and crime, and drugs and crime.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English (Concentration for Teachers)
Requirements: Applicants must have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. Students are not required to submit GRE scores. All applicants must submit a writing sample (10–20 pages in length) of their critical prose, ideally on a literary topic. The writing sample should be suitable for use as a diagnostic tool by faculty evaluating the application. All applicants must submit a personal statement (1–2 pages) indicating their interest in graduate study in English at Kent State University and describing their qualifications for success in the program. Applicants for the M.A. in English (Concentration for Teachers) are also encouraged to submit a current curriculum vitae or resume.
Description:
The Master of Arts in English degree program at Kent State University provides students with advanced study in the fields of literary and cultural criticism, rhetorical and composition studies, creative writing and pedagogy. The program is designed for students who wish to pursue further graduate study leading to the Ph.D. degree or who wish to teach at the secondary or college level.

Graduates of this program will be able to:
*   Demonstrate knowledge of various literary periods, genres, and critical theories.
*   Analyze and interpret complex texts from diverse cultural and historical contexts.
*   Conduct independent research and produce scholarly work in the field of English.
*   Communicate effectively in written and oral forms, demonstrating advanced rhetorical skills.
*   Apply pedagogical theories and practices in teaching English language and literature (for students in the Concentration for Teachers).
CostPerCredit: $616.70/credit hour (Ohio Resident, part-time 1-8 credits, 2023-2024)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English (Literature and Writing)
Requirements:
Applicants to the M.A. in English program (both literature and writing tracks) must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are typically expected to have an undergraduate major in English or in a closely related field. Successful applicants normally have a minimum 3.0 GPA in undergraduate work. While the GRE is not required, applications from students with strong GRE scores are welcome.
Applicants must submit the following materials to the Department of English in addition to the online application:
A Statement of Purpose: Please include a 1-2 page essay describing your academic and professional goals and how the M.A. program in English (Literature and Writing) at Kent State University will help you meet those goals.
A Writing Sample: Please submit a critical essay or an analytical paper of approximately 10-20 pages that demonstrates your ability to analyze literary texts or produce academic prose in a similar field. If you are applying to the Writing Track and have substantial creative writing experience, you may submit a sample of your creative work in lieu of a critical essay (20-25 pages of prose or 8-10 poems).
Three Letters of Recommendation: Letters should be from faculty members or others who can attest to your academic and intellectual abilities.
Transcripts: Upload unofficial transcripts with your online application. Official transcripts are required upon admission.
Fees: Ohio Resident: $7,820.00/Semester; Non-Ohio Resident: $12,522.50/Semester (for 9-18 credit hours)
Fees.1: Ohio Resident: $7,820.00/Semester; Non-Ohio Resident: $12,522.50/Semester (for 9-18 credit hours)
Description: The M.A. in English, Literature and Writing combines focused study in literary history, theory, and criticism with intensive coursework in rhetoric, composition, and creative writing. It provides students with a broad and deep foundation in English studies, as well as the opportunity to specialize and hone their skills in particular areas. The Literature and Writing MA program at Kent State University offers a dynamic and rigorous curriculum designed to cultivate advanced literary and rhetorical understanding and sophisticated writing skills. Our program emphasizes: A comprehensive study of literary history, theory, and criticism. Advanced training in various writing forms, including academic, professional, and creative writing. Opportunities for interdisciplinary study and research. Preparation for further graduate study (Ph.D.) or careers in teaching, publishing, editing, technical writing, and other writing-intensive professions. A diverse and supportive academic community with dedicated faculty mentors.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $738.50/credit hour; Non-Ohio Resident: $1,288.50/credit hour

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching English as a Second Language
Requirements: Applicants for the M.A. in Teaching English as a Second Language program are admitted conditionally or fully, depending on their qualifications and the availability of space in the program. Requirements for admission include: A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. A minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA overall and in the major for full admission. An undergraduate major in English, linguistics, modern and classical language studies, communication, education or a related area (e.g., journalism, philosophy, speech pathology, anthropology, sociology). Minimum 6 semester hours in English grammar. Minimum 6 semester hours in a foreign language (preferably 12 semester hours). Two letters of recommendation from persons familiar with the applicant's academic work and potential for graduate study. A sample of academic writing in English, approximately 5-10 pages long. A brief statement of purpose (1-2 pages) indicating the applicant's academic interests and professional goals related to TESL. Official transcript(s). International applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency through one of the following methods: TOEFL score (minimum 79 iBT, 550 PBT), IELTS score (minimum 6.5), PTE Academic score (minimum 58), Duolingo English Test score (minimum 105), or successful completion of Kent State University's ESL program.
Description: The Master of Arts degree in Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) is designed for students who wish to pursue careers in teaching English to speakers of other languages in the U.S. and abroad, with a particular focus on post-secondary teaching and teacher education. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and pedagogical applications. Students acquire a strong foundation in second language acquisition, linguistics, sociolinguistics, methods of TESL and practical experience through supervised teaching. The program prepares graduates to teach English as a second language, as well as for further graduate studies at the doctoral level.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $608.20/credit hour; Non-Ohio Resident: $1,226.50/credit hour

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts in History program requires an undergraduate major in history or at least 24 semester hours of credit in history. Students whose undergraduate major is not history, but who meet the 24-hour credit requirement may be admitted only with the permission of the graduate coordinator. In addition, students must meet the following minimum requirements:
*   Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA overall or in the last two years of undergraduate study.
*   Official transcript(s)
*   A statement of purpose: explaining the applicant’s academic interests and preparation for graduate study in history.
*   A writing sample: a historical paper of 5-10 pages (no longer than 20 pages) that demonstrates the applicant’s research and analytical abilities.
*   Three letters of recommendation.
*   A curriculum vitae or résumé.
*   International students must meet Kent State University’s English language proficiency requirement.
Description: The Master of Arts in History program is designed for students who wish to deepen their knowledge of history and historical methodology. The program offers advanced study in various historical fields, preparing students for doctoral work, careers in education, public history, or other fields requiring strong research, analytical and communication skills. Students develop a sophisticated understanding of historical processes, interpretations and historiography, and hone their abilities to conduct original research, critically evaluate sources and present their findings effectively.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $553.80/credit; Non-Ohio Resident: $989.20/credit
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Administrative), Fellowships, Tuition Waivers, Merit-based scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Liberal Studies (L.S.M.)
Requirements: To apply to the Master of Liberal Studies program, please submit the following materials through the university's online application system: Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. A statement of purpose outlining academic goals and interests. A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV). A writing sample (e.g., a term paper, essay, or research project from a previous course) that demonstrates the applicant's ability to engage in graduate-level scholarly writing. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic abilities and potential for graduate study. Applicants must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale for undergraduate coursework. International applicants must also meet Kent State University's English language proficiency requirements.
Description: The Master of Liberal Studies (L.S.M.) program at Kent State University is a highly flexible, individualized interdisciplinary graduate program designed for students who want to broaden their knowledge in the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. The L.S.M. is a 30-credit-hour master’s degree program that offers students a wide range of academic choices and opportunities to explore diverse intellectual interests and create a custom-designed curriculum relevant to their personal and professional goals. The program is ideal for students who wish to pursue a graduate degree but whose interests do not fit neatly into one discipline or a traditional master's degree program. It emphasizes critical thinking, intellectual curiosity, and interdisciplinary scholarship, preparing students for diverse career paths or further doctoral study. Students in the L.S.M. program will: Develop advanced critical thinking and analytical skills through exposure to diverse academic disciplines. Cultivate interdisciplinary knowledge and perspectives by integrating insights from the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Enhance research and communication skills through scholarly inquiry and effective presentation of ideas. Prepare for diverse professional opportunities requiring adaptable problem-solving and broad intellectual engagement. Explore new avenues for personal and intellectual growth, fostering a lifelong commitment to learning.
CostPerCredit: $601.50 (Ohio Resident), $1059.50 (Non-Ohio Resident)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Mathematics for Secondary Teachers

Graduates of the program will be better-prepared to teach mathematics courses from Algebra I through calculus, as well as have the background to lead curriculum development within their schools and districts. The program provides the mathematical background needed for a secondary school teacher to earn college credit for teaching dual enrollment courses in high school and fulfills content requirements for licensure renewal.

Requirements: Application deadlines for admission to the Master of Arts (M.A.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Mathematics are July 1 for fall, November 1 for spring and March 1 for summer. A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 in Mathematics courses. A minimum of 24 credit hours of undergraduate mathematics courses at the 30000 level or higher, including a year of advanced calculus/real analysis (MATH 40011/40012) and a semester of abstract algebra (MATH 41001). The GRE General Test is required. Three letters of recommendation are required. A statement of purpose is required. International students must provide evidence of English language proficiency (unless from a country where English is the official language or from an institution where the language of instruction is English).
Description: The Master of Arts in Mathematics degree program develops students' mathematical knowledge and problem-solving abilities. Students choose a concentration in Applied Mathematics, Pure Mathematics or Statistics. Graduates of the program are prepared for doctoral studies in mathematics or statistics, teaching at the community college level or employment in business or industry.

Description: The Spanish M.A. program provides students with advanced knowledge of Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics or Spanish as a second/foreign language. The program prepares students for Ph.D. studies, careers in higher education and secondary education, as well as careers in government and private sectors. Graduates of this program will be able to demonstrate: Advanced proficiency in the Spanish language in all four skill areas (reading, writing, speaking and listening). Advanced knowledge and critical understanding of Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics or Spanish as a second/foreign language. Ability to conduct independent research in the field of Spanish/Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics, or Spanish as a second/foreign language and articulate results both orally and in writing. ProgramName: Master of Arts in Translation
Requirements: Admission to the M.A. in Translation program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. For full admission consideration, applicants should submit the following documents: Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA; Official transcript(s); Curriculum Vitae or Resume; Statement of purpose; Two letters of recommendation; Writing sample; English language proficiency (for international applicants).
Description: The Master of Arts in Translation program provides professional training to prepare students for careers in translation, localization and related fields. It also prepares students who wish to pursue doctoral studies in translation. The program’s main goals are to educate students in translation theory and practice and to develop students’ high-level translation proficiency and cultural competence. The program offers optional concentrations in Literary Translation, Localizing for Global Audiences, Translation for Global Health and Medicine, Translation for Specific Purposes and Translation Studies. The Master of Arts in Translation is a fully online program. The flexible online format allows students to study from any geographic location with a computer and internet access.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $612.90/credit hour, Non-Ohio Resident: $1,114.30/credit hour

Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Physics offers students advanced studies in various areas of theoretical and experimental physics. Students conduct research with faculty and are prepared for doctoral studies or careers in industry. The Department of Physics offers research opportunities in various fields, including astronomy, condensed matter physics, high energy physics, materials science, medical physics, nuclear physics and theoretical physics.
CostPerCredit: Non-Ohio Resident: $1085.60/credit hour, Ohio Resident: $619.90/credit hour

Description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in Physics is offered to students who wish to broaden their knowledge of physics, either as a terminal degree or as preparation for doctoral studies. The program provides a general background in theoretical and experimental physics, with thesis and non-thesis options. Master's degree holders typically find employment in private industry or government laboratories.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science

All applicants must meet the university admission requirements as well as the following program requirements:

*   Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   Submit a curriculum vitae or resume.

Description: The Master of Arts in Political Science program provides students with advanced knowledge of political institutions, processes, and theories. Students develop critical thinking, research, and analytical skills through rigorous coursework, preparing them for careers in government, non-profit organizations, education, and further doctoral studies. The program offers comprehensive training in various subfields of political science, including American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, and public policy. ProgramName: Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.)
Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. Applicants must apply for admission through the Kent State University online application. In addition, applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Statement of purpose (describing professional goals and interest in the M.P.A. degree). Professional resume or curriculum vitae. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. For applicants whose first language is not English, an official TOEFL or IELTS score. Applicants may apply for a waiver of the GRE general test by documenting one of the following: An undergraduate GPA of 3.000 or higher. A master's or doctoral degree from an accredited institution. Description: The Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) degree is an applied professional degree that prepares students for management positions in the public and nonprofit sectors. As a regionally accredited program (NASPAA), the Kent State M.P.A. program provides a broad understanding of the public and nonprofit sectors while developing managerial competencies for effective and ethical leadership. The M.P.A. program emphasizes public policy, public management, analytical methods, financial management and organizational management. Students learn to critically analyze public problems, understand how to implement public policy, manage public programs, develop financial literacy and communicate effectively. All students are required to complete a professional project or thesis.
Accredidation: Regionally accredited program (NASPAA)
CostPerCredit: $816.00/credit hour (Ohio Resident, includes Tuition, General Fee, and College of Arts and Sciences Fee for 1-8 credit hours)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: Students apply through the Kent State University School of Graduate Studies. The requirements are a strong undergraduate record (including some courses in philosophy), three letters of recommendation, a writing sample, a statement of purpose, and a CV. We do not require the GRE. International students must also submit TOEFL/IELTS scores.
Description: A Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in philosophy from Kent State prepares you for further graduate study in philosophy, or for careers where strong analytical skills and clear communication are crucial. Our M.A. program has a strong track record of placing graduates into top Ph.D. programs and teaching positions in philosophy. Students interested in Bioethics and Medical Humanities can pursue the M.A. with a concentration in those areas. The department also participates in the interdisciplinary Medical Humanities Research Group and supports numerous conferences and workshops each year. Our philosophy graduate students have a variety of opportunities to participate in departmental colloquia, conferences, and independent studies with faculty. The department offers a wide range of courses in all the main areas of philosophy, including history of philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, social and political philosophy, philosophy of mind, philosophy of language, and aesthetics.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Clinical Psychology
Description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in Psychological Science prepares students for doctoral work in various areas of psychology (e.g., clinical, cognitive, developmental, experimental, social), and for careers that require research skills (e.g., survey research, program evaluation). Description: The Master of Arts degree in Psychological Sciences offers students advanced training in various areas of psychology. This program provides students with the opportunity to pursue their interests in psychology at an advanced level beyond the undergraduate curriculum. Students will be trained in the scientific method, psychological theory and the application of psychological knowledge through courses in methodology, statistics, theory and practice. There are two concentrations: General and User Experience.

A 3.00 GPA on a 4.00 scale in undergraduate work is usually expected. Students whose undergraduate GPA is less than 3.00 may be admitted conditionally based on other evidence of academic potential, such as a strong statement of purpose, academic letters of recommendation or a professional resume. Students from disciplines other than sociology are welcome to apply. Applicants whose undergraduate major is not in sociology, or a related social science, may be required to take additional undergraduate coursework prior to or concurrently with graduate courses. All applicants are required to submit the following: Official transcripts, A statement of purpose, Three academic letters of recommendation, A professional resume or curriculum vitae.
Department: College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Sociology
Description: The Master of Arts in Sociology degree program provides students with advanced theoretical training, research methods and data analysis skills. The program prepares students for careers in applied social research, teaching at the community college level or further graduate study in a Ph.D. program. The program offers a thesis and a non-thesis option. The thesis option is designed for students considering further graduate work beyond the master’s degree. The non-thesis option is designed for students seeking careers in applied social research or teaching at the community college level. Both options require a comprehensive examination.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $665.50; Non-Ohio Resident: $1,155.10; International Non-Resident: $1,165.10 (per credit hour)

A current professional resume or curriculum vitae (CV) that outlines the applicant's work experience, educational background, professional development activities, publications, presentations, and any other relevant accomplishments. The program focuses on instructional design, emerging technologies, multimedia development, data analysis, and leadership in educational technology. Through hands-on projects, research, and practical experiences, students learn to integrate technology effectively to enhance teaching and learning, foster innovation, and address contemporary educational challenges. ProgramName: Master of Science in Exercise Physiology

The program also provides a strong foundation for those pursuing doctoral studies in exercise physiology or related fields.

Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, research institutions, and various health-related fields. ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Higher Education Administration

A minimum 3.000 cumulative master's degree GPA is required for admission. All applicants must complete the online application, which requires submission of the following materials: Application for Graduate Admission, Official Transcripts, Three Letters of Recommendation, Resume/Curriculum Vitae, Statement of Purpose, Official GRE Scores, Writing Sample, Interview.
Department: College of Education, Health and Human Services
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Higher Education Administration prepares students to serve in administrative and leadership positions in a variety of postsecondary institutions. The program helps students develop a comprehensive understanding of theory and research related to college students, faculty, organization, leadership, finance, governance, and policy. Students learn to apply higher education research and scholarship to practice and policy issues in their professional roles. The program prepares students to become researchers through comprehensive coursework in research methods and quantitative and qualitative research. Students also develop expertise in an area of concentration through their coursework and dissertation research.
CostPerCredit: $638.00/Credit Hour (Ohio Resident Graduate)

ProgramName: Education Specialist in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs
Requirements: To apply for the Ed.S. degree in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs, you must meet the following requirements and complete the online application process. A completed application to the College of Graduate Studies, which includes a personal goal statement, a current resume/curriculum vitae (CV), three letters of recommendation and official transcripts. Master's degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts must be sent to the College of Graduate Studies. An undergraduate GPA of 3.00 on a 4.00 scale and a graduate GPA of 3.50 on a 4.00 scale for unconditional admission.

The Ed.S. program is for individuals who have already earned a master's degree in higher education or a related field and want to build advanced knowledge and leadership skills for higher education administration practice. This program requires 30 credit hours beyond the master’s degree and can be completed in two to three years of study.

A brief (1-3 page) writing sample is required, but it does not need to be a formal research paper (e.g., a paper from an undergraduate class or a professional memorandum).

Requirements:

*   A minimum 3.00 GPA on a 4.00 scale for graduate coursework.
*   Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.

Through a blend of rigorous coursework, hands-on projects, and a culminating dissertation, students will develop advanced critical thinking, research, and communication skills essential for addressing contemporary challenges in their respective professions. The program is designed for working professionals seeking to advance their careers and make a significant impact in areas such as healthcare, education, non-profit management, public service, and business. Graduates of the Ed.D. in Interprofessional Leadership program will be equipped to: Lead diverse teams and foster collaborative environments; Design and implement innovative solutions to complex organizational challenges; Apply ethical principles and social justice perspectives to leadership practices; Conduct rigorous research to inform decision-making and drive continuous improvement; Advocate for systemic change and contribute to the advancement of their fields.

In addition to the university's general graduate admission requirements, applicants must meet the following program-specific requirements: Baccalaureate Degree: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. GPA: A minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA on a 4.000 point scale for undergraduate coursework. Applicants with a GPA below 3.000 but above 2.750 may be considered for conditional admission. Statement of Purpose: A well-written statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) outlining the applicant's academic and professional background, research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing the M.A. in Learning Science. Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic abilities, research potential, and suitability for graduate study. At least one letter should be from a faculty member. Transcripts: Official transcripts from all previously attended institutions. The program focuses on understanding how humans learn and developing instructional innovations that apply learning science principles. It provides students with advanced knowledge and skills in learning theory, research methods, and design of learning environments. The curriculum emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach, drawing from cognitive psychology, educational psychology, computer science, and instructional design. Graduates are prepared for a variety of roles in education, training, corporate learning and development, and research settings.

Students in this program will study how people learn in different contexts. They will learn how to design, implement, and evaluate learning environments, experiences, and technologies to improve learning outcomes. Graduates of the program will address complex problems through the application of advanced research methods and theoretical perspectives grounded in the learning sciences. The Learning Science Ph.D. program provides students with the opportunity to: Engage in the systematic study of learning across various contexts. Acquire skills in designing, implementing, and evaluating learning environments. Develop advanced research methodologies and theoretical frameworks. Contribute to the field of learning sciences through scholarly research and publications. Prepare for leadership roles in academia, research, and educational development.

Students with degrees in unrelated areas are still eligible for admission consideration, but may be required to complete specific undergraduate coursework with a grade of "B" or better prior to or concurrent with graduate study. Students in the program also develop critical thinking, communication and problem-solving skills necessary for professional success.

The program is committed to developing culturally competent school psychologists who utilize prevention and intervention services. The program is designed to integrate the scientific and professional practice knowledge bases to provide a comprehensive training experience. Students apply and integrate coursework in the preparation of school psychology best practices in supervised clinical field experiences.

This program is for individuals interested in professional practice as a school psychologist. Students develop competencies in assessment, intervention, consultation, program development and evaluation. Through extensive supervised practice in school settings, students learn to apply psychological principles to educational issues concerning learning, behavior, social-emotional development and mental health. The program requires 78 credit hours of graduate coursework, including an internship. Graduates of the Ed.S. program meet the academic requirements for licensure as a school psychologist in Ohio and are eligible for the Nationally Certified School Psychologist (NCSP) credential through the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP). Department: College of Education, Health and Human Services
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in School Psychology prepares doctoral students for advanced professional practice as psychologists in school and other settings. The program is committed to a scientist-practitioner model of training that fosters both research and practice competencies. The program provides students with broad and general training in psychology and school psychology, and prepares them for leadership roles in the field. Students typically pursue either the APA-accredited general school psychology training program or a neuropsychology subspecialty track within the school psychology program. The program follows a cohort model and provides students with a sequence of integrated courses and experiences grounded in current theory, research and practice. Faculty are dedicated to providing students with high quality instruction and professional supervision in research, assessment, intervention, consultation and prevention across multiple ecological levels. The program promotes an understanding of diversity issues and culturally sensitive practice in all aspects of its training model. Students complete required coursework, research experience, practica, a dissertation and an internship. Graduates of the program are eligible for licensure as psychologists in Ohio and other states, as well as licensure as school psychologists.
Accredidation: Accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA)

Graduates of the D.N.P. program are prepared to translate evidence into practice, apply evidence-based knowledge and implement programs to improve healthcare outcomes, assume leadership roles in the healthcare system and demonstrate competence in advanced nursing practice.

ProgramName: Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (D.P.M.)
Requirements:
To be considered for admission to the College of Podiatric Medicine, applicants must meet the following minimum requirements:
*   A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university prior to matriculation.
*   Completion of all prerequisite courses with a grade of "C" or better.
*   Minimum GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale (both cumulative and science) is preferred. The average GPA of admitted students is 3.29.
*   Successful completion of the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) within three years of matriculation.

Additional Admission Requirements:
A completed Application for Admission to the College of Podiatric Medicine (CPM).
A personal statement.
Official Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Official MCAT Scores.
Three letters of recommendation (1 from a pre-professional committee or academic advisor, 1 from a science faculty member, and 1 from a practicing DPM or healthcare professional).
Completion of the following pre-requisite courses with a grade of "C" or better within the last seven years:
    Biology (with lab) 8 semester hours / 12 quarter hours
    General Chemistry (with lab) 8 semester hours / 12 quarter hours
    Organic Chemistry (with lab) 8 semester hours / 12 quarter hours (4 hours can be Biochemistry)
    Physics (with lab) 8 semester hours / 12 quarter hours
    English/Communication/Humanities 6 semester hours / 9 quarter hours
    Social Sciences 6 semester hours / 9 quarter hours
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university prior to matriculation.
A successful interview with the Admissions Committee.
Description: Podiatric Medicine is a branch of the medical sciences devoted to the study of human movement in health and disease and the care of the human foot, ankle, and related structures of the leg. It requires a doctor of podiatric medicine (D.P.M.) degree. As an integral member of the healthcare delivery team, the podiatric physician and surgeon is educated and trained to diagnose and treat conditions affecting the foot, ankle, and structures of the leg. This includes conditions related to bone, joints, ligaments, muscles, tendons, nerves, skin, and nails. Podiatrists provide both medical and surgical treatment options, including the prescription of medication, physical therapy, orthotics, prosthetics, and advanced surgical procedures. Podiatrists care for patients of all ages, from infants to the elderly. Podiatric physicians are trained in four years of graduate-level education at one of eleven colleges of podiatric medicine (CPM's) in the United States. Following the D.P.M. degree, all graduates enter into a post-graduate residency program, which are typically 3 years in length. There are a variety of residency programs including Podiatric Medicine and Surgery (PMSR), with or without Reconstructive Rearfoot and Ankle (RRA) credentials. The completion of a residency is required for board certification and to practice in most states. D.P.M.'s work in hospitals, private practice, academic institutions, and federal government agencies. Their patient populations include athletes, diabetics, and pediatric patients. Many podiatrists specialize in surgery, wound care, sports medicine, or biomechanics. Approximately 8% of podiatrists are women.
ScholarshipAmount: $1.7 million annually (College-wide)

The program emphasizes the development of research skills through doctoral seminars and independent study with faculty, and requires students to apply quantitative and analytical methods to issues in financial theory and practice. Students specialize in research in areas such as corporate finance, asset pricing, investments, financial institutions, and derivatives. In addition to rigorous coursework, students are expected to make significant progress on their dissertations throughout the program. Graduates from our program have successfully secured positions at reputable academic institutions globally, reflecting the quality and rigor of our training.

Our fully online program provides a strong foundation in the core values and practices of the LIS profession, while also offering opportunities for specialization in high-demand areas. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, preparing graduates to adapt to the evolving information landscape.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Nursing

Applicants must meet general requirements for admission to the College of Nursing and the Graduate School, as well as specific requirements for the Ph.D. in Nursing program. All applicants must submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. All applicants must meet the following criteria: Baccalaureate and master’s degrees from an accredited college or university. A master’s degree in nursing is preferred but applicants with a master’s degree in a related field who hold a baccalaureate degree in nursing and current, unencumbered RN licensure will be considered on an individual basis. Minimum 3.0 GPA for undergraduate work and a minimum 3.5 GPA for master’s work. Applicants with a cumulative master’s GPA below 3.5 may be considered on an individual basis for conditional admission. Current, unencumbered RN licensure in at least one state in the United States. Evidence of scholarly writing (e.g., published article, master’s thesis, major course paper). Curriculum vitae (CV). Statement of purpose, including short and long-term professional goals and how the Ph.D. program will help in achieving these goals. Three professional letters of recommendation. Description: The College of Nursing offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Nursing degree that provides a program of study for individuals who wish to pursue a career as a nurse scientist in academic or research settings. Graduates of the program are prepared to conduct research and contribute to the development of nursing science and practice. The curriculum prepares graduates to assume leadership roles as researchers, educators, policymakers, and administrators, and to advance health in their chosen area of focus through independent and collaborative research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's or master's degree from an accredited institution in chemistry or a closely related field. Minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA. Official transcripts. Official GRE scores. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose. Resume or curriculum vitae. International applicants are required to have a minimum English language proficiency score.

The program provides the necessary research skills to become leaders in their field. Students develop strong research skills through hands-on participation in experimental or theoretical research in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical education, inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry and polymer chemistry. Graduates are prepared for careers in teaching, research and other chemical endeavors.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics
Requirements: Admission to the Doctor of Philosophy degree program in Physics is contingent upon a review of the applicant's prior academic record and the recommendation of the faculty of the Department of Physics. GRE General Test scores are required. The department code is 6377. International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency by submitting a TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic score. Applicants are admitted into the program only if the department can provide adequate faculty supervision in the applicant’s area of interest and if the department can provide financial support. In addition to applying for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy in Physics program, applicants must also submit the following directly to the Department of Physics: (1) a statement of purpose for seeking the Ph.D. in Physics, (2) two or three letters of recommendation and (3) a list of physics courses taken and textbooks used.
Description: The Ph.D. in Physics prepares students for careers in research and development in industrial, governmental and academic laboratories, or for careers in teaching. The program provides doctoral students with a broad and deep understanding of physics, and the research experience to become independent, creative and critical thinkers. The program emphasizes problem-solving skills, both theoretical and experimental, and the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly, both orally and in writing. Doctoral students are required to conduct original research that makes a significant contribution to their field and to present and defend their dissertation.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health
Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. An earned master's degree from an accredited institution in public health or a health-related field. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA. Minimum 3.500 graduate GPA. A curriculum vitae (CV). A goal statement (maximum three pages) describing applicant's educational and career goals, including how the Ph.D. in Public Health degree aligns with the goals. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can assess applicant's academic abilities, research potential and professional and personal qualities pertinent to success in a doctoral program. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) sent directly from Educational Testing Service (ETS). The GRE General Test requirement may be waived for applicants who hold a terminal master's or doctoral degree (e.g., JD, MBA, MD, MS, Pharm.D.) or an earned master’s degree in Public Health (MPH) from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 3.500. Applicants must still submit official GRE scores if the GPA for their master’s degree is below 3.500. International applicants must have a minimum 83 TOEFL iBT (or equivalent).
Description: The Ph.D. in Public Health program prepares graduates for careers in research, teaching and administration within academia, government and public and private sector organizations. The program emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach to critical public health issues, building a foundation in the core public health disciplines and allowing students to specialize through one of the five concentrations offered in the College of Public Health.
Accredidation: The College of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH) for a seven-year term, extending to July 1, 2027.

All applicants are required to submit the following materials: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume, A statement of purpose (approximately 1,000 words in length) describing academic background, research interests, career goals and the reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in Sociology at Kent State University, A writing sample (an article, thesis chapter or research paper written in English, preferably on a sociological topic, up to 30 pages in length), International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. To enable students to conduct independent research, publish their research findings in academic journals and present their findings at professional conferences.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music Composition

Glauser School of Music requires a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA (on a 4.000 point scale) in the last 60 semester hours of undergraduate coursework, in addition to the following items: Completed online application and application fee. Students in the M.A. program work with faculty mentors on a variety of projects, including theses, concerts, papers, and presentations, depending on the chosen area of concentration. Students in the Composition concentration receive advanced training in music composition, focusing on the development of a distinctive creative voice in various genres and styles. The program culminates in a graduate recital of original compositions or a written thesis.

Description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in Studio Art provides an advanced course of study that offers students the opportunity for focused studio activity in combination with academic coursework in art history and related studies. The program is designed for students seeking to deepen their knowledge, skills and creative expression in a specific studio discipline. The M.A. in Studio Art is a 30-credit-hour program that typically takes two academic years of full-time study to complete. Students applying to the Master of Arts in Studio Art must hold a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Studio Art or a Bachelor of Arts in Art with a studio concentration, or equivalent. The M.A. in Studio Art is offered with concentrations in Ceramics, Drawing, Glass, Jewelry/Metals/Enamel, Painting, Photography, Print Media, Sculpture and Expanded Media, and Textiles. This program is well-suited for individuals interested in careers such as art education, community art programming, gallery management, or pursuing further graduate study (e.g., M.F.A. degree). Graduates of the program will possess enhanced artistic skills, a developed personal artistic vision, and a strong understanding of contemporary art practices and critical theory.

The program offers a core curriculum covering knowledge management principles, practices, and technologies. Students can further specialize through areas of emphasis tailored to their career goals and interests, ensuring a highly relevant and personalized educational experience. Students in the Knowledge Management program develop strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, preparing them to lead and manage knowledge initiatives in diverse organizational settings.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nursing (M.S.N.)
Requirements:
Admission Requirements:
Application to the M.S.N. program is competitive and meeting minimum criteria does not guarantee admission.

To be considered for admission into the M.S.N. program, applicants must meet the following requirements:
*   B.S.N. from an accredited program (ACEN, CCNE, CNEA).
*   Minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
*   Current, unrestricted RN license to practice in Ohio (or eligibility to obtain a license).
*   Evidence of successful completion of a 3-credit undergraduate statistics course. If an applicant has not completed a 3-credit undergraduate statistics course, they may be provisionally admitted if they enroll in an acceptable statistics course during their first semester of graduate study.
*   Evidence of successful completion of a 3-credit undergraduate health assessment course.
*   One year of clinical experience as a registered nurse for those applying to the Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, and Nurse Educator concentrations. Clinical experience requirements for other concentrations vary by concentration.
*   Demonstrate ability to communicate in English if English is not the applicant's native language. See Kent State University's English Language Proficiency Requirements for Graduate Admissions.

Application Requirements:
Applicants must submit the following through the online application system:
*   Official Transcripts
*   Current unencumbered Ohio RN License
*   Curriculum Vitae or Resume
*   Statement of Purpose
*   Three Professional Letters of Recommendation
*   English Language Proficiency Scores (if applicable)
*   Application Fee ($45 domestic / $70 international)
Concentration: Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Nurse Educator, Nursing Administration and Health Systems Leadership, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
Description: As a Master of Science in Nursing (M.S.N.) student at Kent State, you’ll earn a degree that will take your career to the next level and open new doors for advanced practice. In an advanced practice role, you will diagnose and treat acute and chronic illnesses, serve as a primary care provider, specialize in particular populations, and more. Our M.S.N. program emphasizes evidence-based practice, informatics, and leadership. We prepare nurses to practice in complex and dynamic healthcare environments, improve patient outcomes, and transform healthcare systems. With four different advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) concentrations and two advanced nursing practice concentrations, you can pursue the path that’s right for you.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Nursing (M.S.N.) program at Kent State University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).
CostPerCredit: 941.81/credit hour (Ohio Resident), 1,571.60/credit hour (Non-Resident)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Mathematics
Requirements: To be considered for admission, first-year applicants must submit a completed online application, official high school transcripts, and a nonrefundable application fee of $50. ACT or SAT scores are OPTIONAL for admission consideration for most Kent State undergraduate programs, including Actuarial Mathematics.
Department: Department of Mathematical Sciences, College of Arts and Sciences
Fees: Ohio Resident: $6,231.50/Semester; Non-Ohio Resident: $11,029.50/Semester (Academic Year 2023-2024 for full-time undergraduate)
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Mathematics at Kent State University provides students with a strong foundation in mathematics, statistics, and finance, essential for a career as an actuary. The curriculum covers topics such as probability, statistics, financial mathematics, economics, and actuarial models, preparing students for the preliminary exams of the Society of Actuaries (SOA) and the Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS). The program emphasizes practical skills through courses in statistical software and real-world applications. Graduates are well-prepared for entry-level positions in insurance companies, consulting firms, government agencies, and other organizations requiring actuarial expertise. Additionally, the program prepares students for graduate studies in actuarial science or related quantitative fields. Our dedicated faculty members, many of whom are credentialed actuaries, provide individualized attention and mentorship, helping students achieve their academic and professional goals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Africana Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of Africana peoples and cultures in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America and the United States. The program exposes students to critical thinking, reading and writing in several academic areas (humanities, social sciences and the arts). Africana Studies helps students to connect historical and contemporary issues; to develop a global perspective; and to appreciate cultural diversity. The program provides the necessary knowledge and skills for graduates to succeed in the 21st century.
CostPerCredit: 561.90/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Air Traffic and Airspace Management
Requirements: Admission to the Air Traffic Control and Airspace Management (ATC-ATM) program requires acceptance to Kent State University. To be considered for admission to Kent State University, prospective freshmen should submit: an official high school transcript and an application for admission. While ACT/SAT scores are not required for admission to Kent State University, they are required for consideration for many scholarships and for direct admission to some academic programs within the university.
Description: The Air Traffic and Airspace Management B.S. degree provides students with a strong foundation in aviation management, air traffic control and flight operations. Graduates of this program will be prepared for a career as an air traffic controller, or other careers in aviation management and flight operations. The Air Traffic and Airspace Management program is approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under Title 14 CFR Part 65 for air traffic control training. Graduates of this program will receive a letter of accomplishment that may reduce the length of air traffic control training at the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City.
Accredidation: Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under Title 14 CFR Part 65 for air traffic control training.
CostPerCredit: Ohio Resident: $519.25/Credit Hour, Non-Ohio Resident: $1,077.25/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language (ASL) is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a thorough grounding in ASL linguistics, deaf culture and the history of the deaf community. The program is designed to provide students with the linguistic and cultural competency necessary for success in careers that involve working with deaf individuals and the deaf community, as well as prepare them for further graduate study in ASL linguistics, deaf studies, interpreting and other related fields. Students will develop proficiency in ASL and learn about various aspects of deaf culture, including its history, values, and social norms. Students will also gain an understanding of the linguistic features of ASL, including its phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. The program offers opportunities for experiential learning through interaction with the deaf community and service-learning projects. Overall, the BA in ASL program aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and cultural awareness necessary to become effective communicators and advocates for the deaf community.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in American Sign Language/English Interpreting
Requirements: To be considered for admission to Kent State University, students must graduate from an accredited high school or possess a GED certificate. We expect students to have completed a college preparatory curriculum in high school. Kent State uses a holistic review process for first-year admission applicants. This means we review all credentials to gain a full understanding of the applicant's academic preparedness and potential contributions to the university. Test scores (ACT/SAT) are not required, but students are encouraged to submit them for scholarship and course placement consideration.
Department: College of Education, Health and Human Services
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in American Sign Language/English Interpreting prepares students for professional careers as interpreters in a wide range of settings, including educational, legal, medical, mental health, business, employment and video relay services.
This program develops fluency in American Sign Language and spoken English, as well as an understanding of the cultural characteristics of both the Deaf and hearing communities. Students also learn interpreting theory, ethics and professional standards and develop the interpreting skills necessary to work between these two languages and cultures. Graduates of the program are well-prepared to take the national certification examination for interpreters.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animation Game Design
Requirements: The Kent State University website for the Bachelor of Science in Animation Game Design program directs applicants to the general Admissions website for application information. The general freshman admission requirements state: "Admission to Kent State University is selective. When reviewing applications, we look for students who have a strong college preparatory curriculum and solid academic performance. An overall minimum 2.500 GPA on a 4.000 scale is required for admission. Students who fall below the minimum GPA will be reviewed on an individual basis."
Description: The Animation Game Design (AGD) B.S. degree is for students interested in a career in the interactive entertainment industry focusing on the artistic and aesthetic elements of games, or in the fields of animation, interactive media and simulation. The AGD curriculum allows students to develop the aesthetic and technical skills needed to create engaging and impactful games, interactive experiences and animations. Graduates with the AGD degree find careers in the gaming industry as designers, artists, animators and producers. In addition, the AGD degree prepares students for careers in 3D animation, interactive media, simulation, architectural visualization and other visual effects related fields. Graduates also pursue graduate school to further their education.
